# Blocks world (world-blocks): Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `world-blocks.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.34) and `world-blocks-rules.soar` (11 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . world-blocks.soar --seed 1 --cap 200000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . world-blocks.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py world-blocks init-blocksworld2.world

`gen.py` regenerates the rules (`tools/rosie_tasks.py`, function `blocks_world`); `python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with
another example state as the initial world, for the state checks.

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, library v2.34, 16 Nov 2026)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states | init-blocksworld2: goal false; final-blocksworld2: goal true |
| Seeds 1-3, library defaults | solved, 4 moves each (the shortest), 3,288 / 1,373 / 2,870 decisions (the same as blocks-world: only the colors differ) |
| Independent replay | every move legal, goal holds |
| Settings probe (P6) | operator depth: 12 moves over 3 seeds, 7,528 decisions; tie-impasse not measured (see blocks-world). Library defaults kept |

## Assumption ledger (places where the English is open)

| ID | Reading |
|---|---|
| A-H1 | "clear" is defined for a location ("If a location is not below an object") but used for "a clear block". Read as: any object that is not below an object is clear. |
| A-H4 | "move X onto Y": X's on relation and the matching below relation now name Y; the object X left becomes clear. |
| A-B1 | "a blue block is on a purple block and the blue block is below a yellow block": the same blue block in both parts; any blocks of those colors (the world has one of each). |
| A-B2 | The action has no name in the dialog; it is called `move`. |

Convention notes: `clear` is a maintained one-argument relation; the goal is one positive elaboration on the task object.
